title: Bank Deposit Cancellation and Refund Timing Terms
content:
These are the Bank Deposit tier figures that govern a customer's cancellation of a transfer and the time Paloma takes to issue a refund that is owed.

## Figures by tier

| Tier | Full-refund window (hours after booking) | Share of the transfer fee refunded on a cancellation after the window, before release (percent) | Cancellable while in transit | Refund issued within (Paloma business days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bank Deposit Economy | 0.50 (30 minutes) | 100 | yes | 3 |
| Bank Deposit Standard | 0.50 (30 minutes) | 100 | yes | 3 |
| Bank Deposit Express | 0.50 (30 minutes) | 0 | no | 1 |
| Bank Deposit Express Plus | 0.50 (30 minutes) | 50 | no | 1 |
| Bank Deposit Large Amount | 0.50 (30 minutes) | 100 | yes | 2 |
| Bank Deposit International Wire | 0.50 (30 minutes) | 0 | no | 3 |

## Definitions

- **Full-refund window.** The elapsed hours after the booking moment within which a cancellation refunds the principal and every fee in full. It is the Regulation E 30-minute cancellation right, expressed in hours.
- **Share refunded after the window.** The share of the transfer fee refunded when a transfer not yet released is cancelled after the full-refund window.
- **Cancellable while in transit.** Whether a released transfer may still be cancelled before the beneficiary bank credits it.
- **Refund timing.** The Paloma business days within which a refund owed to the customer must be issued, counted from the day it becomes owed.

## Reading the table

Every tier gives the same 30-minute full-refund window. The tiers differ after the window: Economy, Standard and Large Amount return the whole transfer fee on a cancellation before release, Express Plus returns half of it, and Express and International Wire return none of it. Only the three local batch tiers (Economy, Standard and Large Amount) may still be cancelled once released.
